name: vwap_relative_strength_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Comparing a stock's deviation from its VWAP to NIFTY 50's deviation from its VWAP reveals relative strength/weakness. If a stock is above its VWAP by 0.5% while NIFTY is below its VWAP, the stock is showing genuine relative strength — institutional buying is concentrated in that stock despite broad market weakness. This relative VWAP strength predicts continuation because funds rotating capital tend to do so over hours, not minutes. The edge exists because standard relative strength (RS line) uses price ratios, not VWAP-normalized deviations, and misses the volume-weighted institutional flow information that VWAP provides.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND member of a sector with >=5 NIFTY200 stocks

long.confirmation: relative_vwap_strength increasing for 3+ consecutive bars AND stock close > EMA(close, 9)

short.confirmation: relative_vwap_strength decreasing for 3+ consecutive bars AND stock close < EMA(close, 9)

exit.target: 0.6% from entry (ride the relative strength wave)
exit.stop_loss: 0.3% from entry OR relative_vwap_strength crosses zero (lost relative edge)
exit.signal_exit: exit if relative_vwap_strength reverts toward zero (convergence)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if relative_vwap_strength > 1.0 (strong signal)

filters.vix_filter: no specific VIX filter — relative strength works across regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need 45 bars of data) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs on days where NIFTY is range-bound (not >1% trend), as relative strength is more meaningful
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has stock-specific news driving the relative strength (not flow-driven)
other_filters: filter out F&O stocks on expiry day (relative strength distorted by rollover)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — relative VWAP strength is not a standard metric in any platform or screener

weaknesses: Requires real-time NIFTY 50 VWAP computation alongside stock VWAP — double the data infrastructure
Relative strength can flip quickly if sector rotation occurs mid-day (e.g., IT to banks)
In strong market trend days (>1.5% NIFTY move), all stocks move together and relative strength signals are noise
prior_art: Relative Strength (Mansfield, IBD RS rating) is well-established for daily timeframes. Intraday relative strength using VWAP-normalized deviations is less documented. Brian Shannon discusses relative VWAP visually but not as a quantitative signal. Sector rotation momentum is related (Faber, 2007) but on longer horizons.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 60bps - 0.48 * 37.5bps = 31.2 - 18 = 13.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 2.2 bps per trade. Low but positive. Strategy shines when there is genuine sector rotation within the day. Best performance expected on days with mixed sector moves, not broad risk-on/off days.
